content_html:
The Cusco Festivities are one of the most important cultural celebrations in Peru. Every year during the month of June, Cusco revives its Inca history and cultural identity through parades, music, traditional dances, and ancestral ceremonies.

The city of Cusco, the former capital of the Inca Empire, fills with color, tradition, and cultural pride, attracting thousands of visitors from around the world.

During these weeks, plazas, streets, and historic centers become stages where communities, institutions, and cultural groups celebrate Andean heritage.

Why Experience the Cusco Festivities

  • Unique cultural celebrations in the Andes
  • Traditional dances and typical costumes
  • Music, parades, and ancestral ceremonies

Inti Raymi: The Great Festival of the Sun

Inti Raymi is the main event of the Cusco Festivities and takes place every June 24.

This impressive historical reenactment revives the ancient Inca ceremony dedicated to the Sun God, one of the most important celebrations of the Inca Empire.

The performance takes place at three historic locations:

  • Qorikancha
  • Plaza de Armas de Cusco
  • Sacsayhuamán

Thousands of people attend every year to witness this unique cultural spectacle.

What Makes Inti Raymi Special

  • Historical reenactment of the Inca Empire
  • Participation of hundreds of actors and dancers
  • Stunning archaeological settings

Traditional Parades and Dances in Plaza de Armas

Throughout June, schools, communities, and organizations participate in colorful cultural parades.

Most performances take place in Plaza de Armas de Cusco, where thousands gather to enjoy the spectacle.

Each group presents traditional dances representing different regions of Cusco and Peru.

What You’ll See in the Parades

  • Traditional colorful costumes
  • Choreographies with Andean music
  • Cultural performances from various communities

Traditional Gastronomy During the Festivities

The celebrations are also a perfect opportunity to enjoy Cusco’s gastronomy.

One of the most representative dishes of this season is Chiriuchu, considered the emblematic dish of the Cusco Festivities.

This dish combines traditional ingredients from different Andean regions.

Flavors You Can Try

  • Traditional Chiriuchu
  • Roast guinea pig (Cuy al horno)
  • Tamales and humitas
  • Traditional Andean beverages

Cultural Celebrations Throughout Cusco

The festivities are not limited to the historic center. Throughout June, neighborhoods and communities across the region organize cultural events, concerts, and festivals.

The streets fill with music, dances, and activities celebrating Andean identity.

Activities You Can Enjoy

  • Concerts and cultural performances
  • Artisan fairs
  • Gastronomic events
  • Community celebrations
